available.title: Automatic encrypted backup
available.description: Every ~30 seconds, new or changed files in your backup folder are encrypted on your device and sent to your buddy. Deleting a file locally removes it from your buddy's live copy too (older versions stay recoverable).

available.title: Direct peer-to-peer transfer, with automatic relay fallback
available.description: Your device and your buddy's device try to connect directly first. On the same local network, that's instant and automatic. Over the internet, it depends on both sides' network/router — when a direct connection isn't possible, your data still transfers reliably through our relay, which can never read it (see “Known limitations” below for when this applies).

available.title: Restore, including file history
available.description: Restore a single file, restore everything your buddy has for you at once, or pull back a specific earlier version of a file you've since deleted — with a live progress indicator while it runs.

available.title: Pledge-based storage limits
available.description: Each buddy pairing has an agreed storage size. Going over it is refused automatically, and your dashboard tells you exactly why a file didn't send (pledge full, file too large, buddy's disk full).

available.title: Drift detection (reconciliation)
available.description: Roughly every 10 minutes, your device double-checks that what your buddy actually has on disk still matches what it expects — catching anything lost or changed outside the normal backup flow — and automatically re-sends anything missing.

available.title: Unreachable-buddy detection
available.description: If your buddy's device genuinely can't be reached, your dashboard flags it as stale rather than silently showing “backup ok” — backed by a real connectivity check, not an assumption.

available.title: Dashboard
available.description: Per-buddy backup status, your device's name/build/uptime/local file count, how many buddies are currently visible on your local network, each buddy's real disk usage, and a lifetime direct-vs-relay bandwidth breakdown.

available.title: Find a buddy
available.description: Browse public listings at an exact storage size, with optional self-reported country, upload-speed tier, always-on, and relay-only info to help you judge fit before pairing.

available.title: Free tier
available.description: The first 50GB you pledge to buddies is free, no card required.

available.title: Relay bandwidth billing
available.description: On a paid plan, relay usage (when a direct connection isn't possible) is metered and billed at $0.02/GB, shown as its own line item on your invoice — confirmed end-to-end against real billing.

available.title: Low-disk protection
available.description: Your device refuses incoming files once its own disk runs low (a flat 2GB, or 5% of the disk, whichever's bigger), independent of pledge size — so a buddy's data can never fill your disk to nothing.

available.title: Password reset and account support
available.description: Forgot your password? Use “Forgot password?” on the login page to get a reset link by email. For account, login, billing, or backup questions, use “Contact support” on your dashboard (it sends your account details along, so there's less back-and-forth), or email support@filegarden.net from your account's email address if you can't log in. Resetting your website password never affects your backups: files are encrypted with the passphrase on your own device, which is separate from your account password. That also means nobody, including us, can recover that passphrase if it's lost, so keep it somewhere safe.

limitations.title: Direct connections aren't guaranteed on every network
limitations.description: Whether a direct connection is possible depends on your router/network's NAT behavior. Many home networks and local networks work great. Some networks — strict corporate firewalls especially — block the hole-punching direct connections need entirely, forwarded port or not. When that happens, your backups still complete normally through our relay; this is expected, graceful behavior, not a failure.

limitations.title: Marketplace listing filters
limitations.description: Country, upload speed, “usually online”, and “relay-only” are currently shown on listings to help you judge a buddy yourself, but don't yet filter or auto-match search results.

limitations.title: Fixed backup interval, no file filtering
limitations.description: Backups run on a fixed ~30 second cycle and back up everything in your configured folder — there's no way yet to change the interval or exclude specific files/patterns.

limitations.title: One buddy per pledge
limitations.description: Each pledge is a 1:1 relationship with a single buddy — there's no way to share one backup folder across multiple buddies at once.
